name: Practice (abhyāsa)
method_summary: Repeatedly restraining the mind and bringing it back under control in the self wherever it wanders (6.26); with dispassion, the means by which the restless mind is held (6.35). The practice of a former life carries the fallen yogin on in the next (6.44).

name: Practice and dispassion (abhyāsa and vairāgya)
method_summary: The mind is admittedly restless and hard to restrain, but it is held by practice (abhyāsa) and dispassion (vairāgya) (6.35); yoga is hard to attain for one whose self is unrestrained, but attainable by one who is self-controlled and strives by the proper means (6.36).

warnings.text: Yoga is hard to attain for one whose self is unrestrained (6.36).

notes: Cf. Yoga Sūtra 1.12 (abhyāsa-vairāgyābhyāṃ tan-nirodhaḥ) for the same pair.

name: Non-possessiveness (aparigraha)
method_summary: One who has given up all possessions, without expectation, doing merely bodily action, incurs no fault (4.21); the meditating yogin is to be alone, without expectation and without possessions (6.10).

name: Posture (āsana)
method_summary: In the Gītā āsana is the meditation seat: a firm seat in a clean place, neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, deer-skin and kuśa grass (6.11); seated on it one holds body, head and neck in line and motionless (6.12–13).

name: Seeing others' pleasure and pain as one's own (ātmaupamya)
method_summary: Seeing the same everywhere, pleasure or pain, by comparison with oneself; the yogin who does so is held to be the highest (6.32).

name: Fixing the gaze between the eyebrows (bhrū-madhya)
method_summary: Having put external contacts outside, the gaze (cakṣus) is placed between the eyebrows, and prāṇa and apāna moving within the nostrils are made even; the sage so restrained, intent on liberation and free of desire, fear and anger is forever free (5.27–28). The text gives no further method.
notes: In 6.13 the Gītā instead prescribes gazing toward the tip of the nose; the text does not relate the two instructions.

name: The vow of the celibate student (brahmacāri-vrata)
method_summary: The meditating yogin, tranquil and fearless, is to be firm in the vow of the brahmacārin while sitting with mind restrained and fixed on the Lord (6.14). The text does not spell out the vow.

name: Offering as Brahman (brahmārpaṇa)
method_summary: Performing the offering while seeing each factor as Brahman — the offering or ladle, the oblation, the fire, the offerer — with concentration on action as Brahman; Brahman is what such a one reaches (4.24). Related: acting having placed one's actions in Brahman and abandoned attachment, one is untouched by evil like a lotus leaf by water (5.10).

name: The Gītā's meditation (dhyāna-yoga, BhG 6.10–32)
method_summary: The yogin constantly yokes himself in a secluded place, alone, with mind and self restrained, without expectation or possessions (6.10); on a firm seat in a clean place (6.11), he makes the mind one-pointed, restrains the activity of thought and senses and practises for self-purification (6.12); holding body, head and neck in line and motionless, gazing toward the tip of his nose, not looking about (6.13), tranquil, fearless, in the vow of the brahmacārin, with mind restrained and fixed on and intent on the Lord (6.14). Abandoning all desires born of intention and restraining the senses with the mind (6.24), he comes to rest little by little by an intellect held firm, makes the mind abide in the self and thinks of nothing (6.25); wherever the restless mind wanders he brings it back into the self (6.26).
stage: unmarked in the text (6.3 distinguishes the one wishing to ascend to yoga from the one who has ascended)
prerequisites: moderation in food, recreation, effort, sleep and waking (6.16–17)
signs_of_progress: the controlled mind rests in the self alone, free of longing for any desire (6.18)
like a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker (6.19)
the mind comes to rest; seeing the self by the self one is content in the self (6.20)
boundless happiness grasped by the intellect beyond the senses; not wavering from reality; no greater gain; not shaken by heavy sorrow (6.21–22)
supreme happiness, rajas stilled, becoming Brahman, the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman (6.27–28)
seeing the self in all beings and all beings in the self; seeing the Lord everywhere (6.29–31)
peace culminating in nirvāṇa, abiding in the Lord (6.15)

warnings.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or nothing at all, nor for one who sleeps too much or keeps awake (6.16).
The mind is restless, turbulent and as hard to restrain as the wind (6.34); it is held only by practice and dispassion (6.35).
Yoga is hard to attain for one whose self is unrestrained (6.36).

duration: constantly (satatam 6.10; sadā 6.15, 6.28); perfection may take many births (6.45)
notes: Yoga is defined here as 'the unyoking from union with sorrow', to be practised with resolve and an undejected mind (6.23). One who falls away is not lost: he is reborn and resumes (6.40–45).

name: Sacrifice of material things (dravya-yajña)
method_summary: Sacrifice performed with material things, listed among the kinds of sacrifice (4.28) and declared inferior to the sacrifice of knowledge (4.33).

name: Making prāṇa and apāna even (prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā)
method_summary: Having made even (sama) the prāṇa and apāna that move within the nostrils — together with putting external contacts outside and placing the gaze between the brows (5.27) — the sage with senses, mind and intellect restrained, intent on liberation, is forever free (5.28). The text gives no count, ratio or retention.

name: The meditation seat and posture of the Gītā
method_summary: A firm seat of one's own set up in a clean place, neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, deer-skin and kuśa grass (6.11); seated there the yogin makes the mind one-pointed and practises (6.12), holding body, head and neck in line and motionless, gazing toward the nose-tip (6.13).
notes: Commentators take the layering as kuśa grass beneath, skin above it, cloth on top.

name: Restraint of the senses (indriya-saṃyama)
method_summary: Offering the senses into the fires of restraint (4.26) and the actions of senses and breath into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint kindled by knowledge (4.27); restraint of the senses is a condition for gaining knowledge (4.39); in meditation the whole troop of senses is restrained on every side by the mind (6.24); external contacts are put outside (5.27).
notes: Not the technical saṃyama of Yoga Sūtra 3.4.

name: Sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña)
method_summary: Sacrifice consisting in knowledge (4.28), better than the sacrifice of material things, since all action culminates in knowledge (4.33); the knowledge is to be learnt from truth-seeing knowers approached with prostration, questioning and service (4.34).

name: Karma-yoga: performing required action without attachment to the fruit
method_summary: Doing the action that ought to be done without depending on its fruit (6.1); acting having placed actions in Brahman and abandoned attachment (5.10); acting with body, mind, intellect and senses for self-purification (5.11); giving up the fruit (5.12); acting as the ancient seekers of liberation acted (4.15). Declared superior to the renunciation of action (5.2); for one wishing to ascend to yoga action is the means (6.3).
stage: ārurukṣu — one wishing to ascend to yoga (6.3)
signs_of_progress: not stained though acting, like a lotus leaf by water (5.7, 5.10)

name: Relinquishing the fruit of action
method_summary: Abandoning attachment to the fruit of action, ever content and depending on nothing, one does nothing though engaged in action (4.20); the yoked one who gives up the fruit attains lasting peace, while the unyoked, attached to fruit through desire, is bound (5.12); the renouncer and yogin acts without depending on the fruit (6.1).

name: Gazing toward the tip of the nose (nāsikāgra)
method_summary: Seated with body, head and neck held in line and motionless, the yogin gazes at the tip of his own nose and does not look about in the directions (6.13).
notes: Commentators (e.g. Śaṅkara) read 'saṃprekṣya' as 'as if gazing', i.e. the eyes turned toward the nose-tip rather than fixed on it.

name: Breath as sacrifice: offering prāṇa and apāna
method_summary: Those intent on breath-regulation offer prāṇa into apāna and apāna into prāṇa, restraining the courses of both (4.29); others, regulated in food, offer breaths into breaths (4.30); these count among the sacrifices that destroy impurity (4.30). The text gives no count, ratio or duration.

name: Breath-regulation (prāṇāyāma)
method_summary: Named once in chs. 4–6: those intent on prāṇāyāma offer prāṇa into apāna and apāna into prāṇa, restraining their courses — a form of sacrifice (4.29). Cf. making prāṇa and apāna even in the nostrils (5.27).

name: Approaching the teacher: prostration, inquiry and service
method_summary: Knowledge is learnt by prostration (praṇipāta), thorough questioning (paripraśna) and service (sevā) toward the knowers who see the truth, who will then instruct it (4.34).

name: Renunciation (saṃnyāsa)
method_summary: In chs. 5–6 renunciation is defined inwardly: the constant renouncer neither hates nor craves (5.3); renouncing all actions by the mind the embodied one dwells at ease in the nine-gated city (5.13); the renouncer is one who does required action without depending on its fruit, not one who has merely given up the sacred fires and rites (6.1); what is called renunciation is yoga, i.e. renunciation of intention (6.2).

warnings.text: Renunciation is hard to attain without yoga (5.6).

name: Recitation / study (svādhyāya)
method_summary: Ascetics of strict vows sacrifice through recitation and knowledge (4.28).

name: Austerity (tapas)
method_summary: Sacrifice of austerity is one of the kinds of sacrifice (4.28); many purified by the austerity of knowledge reached the Lord's state (4.10); the Lord is the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities (5.29); the yogin is held greater than the ascetics (6.46).

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: With practice, the means by which the restless, hard-to-restrain mind is held (6.35).

name: Sacrifice (yajña)
method_summary: People sacrifice to deities for quick success of their actions (4.12); acting for the sake of sacrifice, action dissolves (4.23); sacrifice extended to many inner and outer forms (4.24–30), all born of action (4.32); eaters of its remainder go to the eternal Brahman, and the non-sacrificer has neither this world nor the next (4.31); the sacrifice of knowledge is best (4.33); the Lord is the enjoyer of sacrifices (5.29).

name: Measure in food, recreation, effort, sleep and waking (yuktāhāra-vihāra)
method_summary: For one measured in food and recreation, measured in effort in actions, measured in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow (6.17); yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all, nor for one given to too much sleep, nor for one who keeps awake (6.16).

warnings.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all (ekāntam anaśnataḥ), nor for one given to too much sleep or wakefulness (6.16).
